summary: @servicetitan/microfront-utils preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases as a zip, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. math_init.js is a ~720 KB single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle with string-array rotation (`function WV8StW(...){...MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift())...}`), hex-mangled identifiers, and reassembled URL/domain fragments, hiding what actually executes. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern (fetch a second language runtime and execute an obfuscated sibling under it) bypasses Node-oriented inspection of install-time behavior. The dropper's presence and the mismatch between the file `math_init.js` and the advertised microfrontend utility purpose are inconsistent with a legitimate release under the @servicetitan scope and are consistent with a compromised or typosquatted publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
